subject: maths
title: Bar Charts, Pictograms and Tables
seo_title: Year 3 Bar Charts and Pictograms Worksheets: Tally Charts, Tables and How Many More (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Interpret and present data using bar charts, pictograms and tables; solve one-step and two-step questions [for example, ‘How many more?’ and ‘How many fewer?’] using information presented in scaled bar charts and pictograms and tables.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 maths worksheets on statistics: pictograms where one symbol stands for 2, 5 or 10, bar charts with scales of 2, 5 and 10, tally charts and tables, and one-step and two-step “how many more?” and “how many fewer?” questions. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Look at the key or the scale first. Then read the chart.
key_sub: If one symbol = 10, half a symbol = 5. A bar halfway between 10 and 20 shows 15. Altogether means add; how many more or how many fewer means subtract.
body_html:
Three ways to show data

Data is information we collect, such as votes or minibeasts we find. A tally chart or a table shows the numbers. A pictogram or a bar chart lets you compare them at a glance.

Read a pictogram

Look at the key first. One symbol can stand for 2, 5 or 10. Count the symbols in a row in 2s, 5s or 10s. Half a symbol stands for half of the key, not 1.

Example

How many votes did Pear get?

4 circles and half a circle. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, then 1 more for the half.

Answer: 9 votes

If each symbol = 10, half a symbol = 5. Three and a half symbols = 10, 20, 30 and 5 more = 35.

Read a bar chart

First find what the scale goes up in: 2s, 5s or 10s. Then go across from the top of the bar to the scale. If a bar ends halfway between two lines, the number is halfway between them.

Example

How many more pupils have a dog than a rabbit?

Dog: 12. Rabbit: 9. 12 − 9 = 3.

Answer: 3 more pupils

Tally charts and tables

In a tally chart, every fifth mark goes across the other four. Count the groups in 5s, then add the single marks.

In a table, find the right row, then go across to the right column.

MinibeastClass 3AClass 3B
Worms118
Snails613
Example

How many snails did Class 3B find?

Snails row, Class 3B column: 13.

Answer: 13 snails

Add or subtract?

The question saysDo this
altogether, in total, both, A or BAdd
how many more, how many fewer, differenceSubtract

A two-step question needs two sums. Do one step, then use the answer in the next step.

Two-step example

Football got 16 votes. Choir got 7 and Chess got 5. How many more votes did Football get than Choir and Chess together?

Step 1: 7 + 5 = 12. Step 2: 16 − 12 = 4.

Answer: 4 more votes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting symbols, not using the key (4 circles = 4)Use the key: 4 circles of 5 = 20
Saying half a symbol = 1Half a symbol is half of the key: half of 10 is 5
Reading a bar between two lines as the lower lineHalfway between 10 and 20 is 15
Counting grid spaces instead of reading the scaleRead the number on the scale
Counting a tally group of 5 as 4The line across is the fifth mark
Adding when the question says how many moreHow many more means subtract

faq.q: What statistics do children learn in Year 3?
faq.a: In Year 3 children read and draw bar charts, pictograms and tables. They answer one-step and two-step questions such as “How many more?” and “How many fewer?”.

faq.q: How do you read a pictogram with a key?
faq.a: Look at the key first, then count the symbols in 2s, 5s or 10s. Half a symbol is half of the key, so if one circle = 10, half a circle = 5.

faq.q: How do you read a bar chart with a scale of 2, 5 or 10?
faq.a: Find what the scale goes up in, then go across from the top of the bar to the scale. If the bar ends halfway between two lines, the number is halfway between them.

faq.q: What is a two-step problem with a bar chart?
faq.a: It is a question that needs two sums. For example, add two bars together first, then find the difference between that total and a third bar.

items.q: How many blue tits were seen?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle stands for 2 birds. The Blue tit row has 6 circles: 6 × 2 = 12 birds.
Look at the key: each star stands for 5 cakes. The Wed row has 1 star: 1 × 5 = 5 cakes.

items.q: How many cans did class 3A collect?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 10 cans. The 3A row has 5 squares and half a square: 5 × 10 = 50, and half of 10 is 5, so 50 + 5 = 55 cans.

items.q: In this pictogram, what does half a circle stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole circle = 10 points. Half a circle is half of 10, which is 5 points, not 1.
Look at the key: each star stands for 5 books. The Mystery row has 5 stars: 5 × 5 = 25 books.

items.q: Which row shows the most pupils?
items.e: Every square stands for the same number, so the row with the most squares shows the most. The Rabbit row has 6 squares: 6 × 2 = 12 pupils.

items.q: Each star stands for 2 books. Freya read 9 books. How many stars should be in her row?
items.e: Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. 4 whole stars make 8. 1 more is half of 2, so add half a star. Draw 4 and a half stars.
Look at the key: each star stands for 2 pupils. The Swimming row has 3 stars and half a star: 3 × 2 = 6, and half of 2 is 1, so 6 + 1 = 7 pupils.

items.q: In this pictogram, what does half a square stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole square = 10 votes. Half a square is half of 10, which is 5 votes, not 1.

items.q: Which row shows 3 votes?
items.e: Half a circle is 1, so 3 votes is 1 and a half circles. The Pear row has 1 circle and half a circle: 1 × 2 = 2, and half of 2 is 1, so 2 + 1 = 3 votes.
Look at the key: each star stands for 10 pupils. The Bus row has 1 star and half a star: 1 × 10 = 10, and half of 10 is 5, so 10 + 5 = 15 pupils.

items.q: Which row shows the fewest lollies?
items.e: Every square stands for the same number, so the row with the fewest squares shows the fewest. The Orange row has 2 squares: 2 × 5 = 10 lollies.

items.q: Each circle stands for 10 pupils. 45 pupils walk to school. How many circles should be in the Walk row?
items.e: Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40. 4 whole circles make 40. 5 more is half of 10, so add half a circle. Draw 4 and a half circles.
Look at the key: each star stands for 5 minibeasts. The Ladybird row has 2 stars: 2 × 5 = 10 minibeasts.

items.q: How many stickers has Grace got?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 2 stickers. The Grace row has 5 squares and half a square: 5 × 2 = 10, and half of 2 is 1, so 10 + 1 = 11 stickers.

items.q: In this pictogram, what does half a circle stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole circle = 10 books. Half a circle is half of 10, which is 5 books, not 1.
Half a star is 5, so 45 lollies is 4 and a half stars. The Cherry row has 4 stars and half a star: 4 × 10 = 40, and half of 10 is 5, so 40 + 5 = 45 lollies.

items.q: How many books did Amelia read?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 5 books. The Amelia row has 2 squares: 2 × 5 = 10 books.

items.q: Each square stands for 5 votes. Red got 30 votes. How many squares should be in the Red row?
items.e: Count in 5s until you reach 30: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. That is 6 steps, so draw 6 squares. Check: 6 × 5 = 30.
Look at the key: each star stands for 10 pupils. The Car row has 5 stars and half a star: 5 × 10 = 50, and half of 10 is 5, so 50 + 5 = 55 pupils.

sets.title: Bar charts with scales of 2, 5 and 10

items.q: What does the scale on this bar chart go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 2, 4, 6 … Each line is 2 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 2s.

items.q: How many blackbirds were seen?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Blackbird bar ends on the line for 2. So the answer is 2 birds.

items.q: How many woodlice were found?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Woodlouse bar ends on the line for 30. So the answer is 30 minibeasts.

items.q: How many points did Kestrel House get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Kestrel bar ends halfway between 40 and 50, so it shows 45. So the answer is 45 points.

items.q: How many shells did Alfie find?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Alfie bar ends on the line for 8. So the answer is 8 shells.

items.q: Which bar shows 35 cans?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Find 35 on the scale. The 3B bar ends on the line for 35.

items.q: How many cakes were sold on Tuesday?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Tue bar ends halfway between 40 and 50, so it shows 45. So the answer is 45 cakes.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar chart go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 5, 10, 15 … Each line is 5 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 5s.

items.q: Which bar shows the most pupils?
items.e: The Fish bar is the tallest one. The Fish bar ends on the line for 14. It shows 14 pupils.

items.q: How many votes did Purple get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Purple bar ends halfway between 40 and 50, so it shows 45. So the answer is 45 votes.

items.q: How many votes did Grapes get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Grapes bar ends on the line for 10. So the answer is 10 votes.

items.q: How many books did Harry read?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Harry bar ends halfway between 8 and 10, so it shows 9. So the answer is 9 books.

items.q: Which bar shows the fewest pupils?
items.e: The Car bar is the shortest one. The Car bar ends on the line for 20. It shows 20 pupils.

items.q: How many stickers has Mohammed got?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Mohammed bar ends on the line for 20. So the answer is 20 stickers.

items.q: How many shells did Maya find?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Maya bar ends halfway between 8 and 10, so it shows 9. So the answer is 9 shells.

items.q: Which bar shows 35 cakes?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. Find 35 on the scale. The Wed bar ends halfway between 30 and 40, so it shows 35.

items.q: How many votes did Purple get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Purple bar ends on the line for 60. So the answer is 60 votes.

items.q: Which bar shows the most birds?
items.e: The Sparrow bar is the tallest one. The Sparrow bar ends on the line for 35. It shows 35 birds.

items.q: How many pupils have a fish?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Fish bar ends halfway between 4 and 6, so it shows 5. So the answer is 5 pupils.

items.q: Which bar shows 8 votes?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Find 8 on the scale. The Orange bar ends on the line for 8.

items.q: How many votes did Apple get?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Apple row has 2 groups of 5 and 1 more: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 + 1 = 11.

items.q: How many votes did Grapes get?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Grapes row has 1 group of 5 and 2 more: 1 × 5 = 5, and 5 + 2 = 7.

items.q: How many buses went past the school?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Bus row has 1 group of 5 and 2 more: 1 × 5 = 5, and 5 + 2 = 7.

items.q: Which row shows 8 vehicles?
items.e: 8 = 5 + 3. Look for 1 group of 5 and 3 single marks. That is the Van row.

items.q: How many pupils chose netball?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Netball row has 2 groups of 5 and 4 more: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 + 4 = 14.

items.q: How many pupils are shown in the tally chart altogether?
items.e: Count each row: Football 11, Netball 14, Swimming 13, Cricket 16. Then add: 11 + 14 + 13 + 16 = 54 pupils.

items.q: How many black cars were there?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Black row has 3 groups of 5 and 1 more: 3 × 5 = 15, and 15 + 1 = 16.

items.q: What is the difference between the biggest and the smallest number of cars?
items.e: The biggest is Silver (19). The smallest is Red (12). Difference means subtract: 19 − 12 = 7.

items.q: Which row shows 11 minibeasts?
items.e: 11 = 5 + 5 + 1. Look for 2 groups of 5 and 1 single mark. That is the Spider row.

items.q: How many minibeasts are shown in the tally chart altogether?
items.e: Count each row: Ladybird 18, Worm 8, Snail 4, Spider 11. Then add: 18 + 8 + 4 + 11 = 41 minibeasts.

items.q: How many worms did class 3A find?
items.e: Find the Worms row, then go across to the Class 3A column. The cell says 6.

items.q: How many spiders did the two classes find altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Add the two cells in the Spiders row: 14 + 4 = 18.

items.q: How many more snails did class 3A find than class 3B?
items.e: How many more means find the difference: 18 − 15 = 3.

items.q: Which minibeast did the two classes find the most of altogether?
items.e: Add each row: Ladybirds 5 + 9 = 14, Worms 6 + 17 = 23, Snails 18 + 15 = 33, Spiders 14 + 4 = 18. The biggest total is 33, for snails.

items.q: How many books did Oliver read in week 2?
items.e: Find the Oliver row, then go across to the Week 2 column. The cell says 4.

items.q: How many books did the four pupils read in week 2?
items.e: Add the whole Week 2 column: 4 + 7 + 9 + 6 = 26.

items.q: How many more books did Evie read in week 1 than in week 2?
items.e: How many more means find the difference: 13 − 6 = 7.

items.q: How many pupils had a hot dinner on Tuesday?
items.e: Find the Tuesday row, then go across to the Hot dinner column. The cell says 21.

items.q: How many pupils had lunch on Monday altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Add the two cells in the Monday row: 23 + 18 = 41.

items.q: How many pupils had a hot dinner from Monday to Thursday?
items.e: Add the whole Hot dinner column: 23 + 21 + 17 + 9 = 70.

sets.title: How many more, how many fewer, how many altogether?

items.q: How many more pupils chose netball than swimming?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Netball 9 and Swimming 4. How many more means find the difference: 9 − 4 = 5 pupils.
Each star = 5. Orange 4 × 5 = 20 and Lemon 5 × 5 = 25. Altogether means add: 20 + 25 = 45 lollies.

items.q: How many fewer cans did class 3B collect than 3C?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. 3C 50 and 3B 20. How many fewer means find the difference: 50 − 20 = 30 cans.

items.q: How many more woodlice were found than ladybirds?
items.e: Each circle = 2, so half a circle = 1. Woodlouse 3 × 2 + 1 = 7 and Ladybird 2 × 2 = 4. How many more means find the difference: 7 − 4 = 3 minibeasts.

items.q: How many space and mystery books were borrowed altogether?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Space 5 and Mystery 30. Altogether means add: 5 + 30 = 35 books.

items.q: How many fewer points did Owl House get than Hawk House?
items.e: Each square = 10, so half a square = 5. Hawk 6 × 10 = 60 and Owl 4 × 10 = 40. How many fewer means find the difference: 60 − 40 = 20 points.

items.q: How many books did the pupils read altogether?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Read every bar: Arjun 5, Isla 7, Harry 6, Leo 3. Add them: 5 + 7 + 6 + 3 = 21 books.

items.q: How many more stickers has Mohammed got than Ruby?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Mohammed 25 and Ruby 5. How many more means find the difference: 25 − 5 = 20 stickers.

items.q: How many cans did classes 3C and 3A collect altogether?
items.e: Each square = 10, so half a square = 5. 3C 3 × 10 = 30 and 3A 6 × 10 = 60. Altogether means add: 30 + 60 = 90 cans.

items.q: How many fewer robins were seen than blue tits?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Blue tit 9 and Robin 4. How many fewer means find the difference: 9 − 4 = 5 birds.

items.q: How many more shells did Noah find than Ethan and Maya together?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Noah 30, Ethan 5 and Maya 10. Step 1: Ethan and Maya together: 5 + 10 = 15. Step 2: 30 − 15 = 15 shells.

items.q: How many stickers have they got altogether?
items.e: Each square = 5. Read every row: Mohammed 3 × 5 = 15, Kai 4 × 5 = 20, Grace 2 × 5 = 10, Ruby 1 × 5 = 5. Add them: 15 + 20 + 10 + 5 = 50 stickers.

items.q: How many more cakes were sold on Wednesday than on Tuesday?
items.e: Each circle = 10, so half a circle = 5. Wed 5 × 10 = 50 and Tue 2 × 10 + 5 = 25. How many more means find the difference: 50 − 25 = 25 cakes.
Each star = 2, so half a star = 1. Yellow 4 × 2 + 1 = 9, Red 3 × 2 = 6 and Green 3 × 2 + 1 = 7. Step 1: Red and Green together: 6 + 7 = 13. Step 2: 13 − 9 = 4 votes fewer.

items.q: The school wants to sell 200 cakes altogether. How many more cakes must it sell?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. Step 1: read every bar and add: 60 + 30 + 40 + 50 = 180. Step 2: 200 − 180 = 20 cakes.

items.q: How many more pupils chose football than rugby and swimming together?
items.e: Each circle = 10, so half a circle = 5. Football 4 × 10 + 5 = 45, Rugby 1 × 10 = 10 and Swimming 1 × 10 + 5 = 15. Step 1: rugby and swimming together: 10 + 15 = 25. Step 2: 45 − 25 = 20 pupils.
Each star = 5. Sport 6 × 5 = 30 and Space 4 × 5 = 20. How many fewer means find the difference: 30 − 20 = 10 books.

items.q: How many fewer votes did Orange get than Banana and Pear together?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. Orange 40, Banana 20 and Pear 30. Step 1: Banana and Pear together: 20 + 30 = 50. Step 2: 50 − 40 = 10 votes fewer.

items.q: The pupils want to read 100 books altogether this term. How many more books must they read?
items.e: Each circle = 5. Step 1: read every row and add: 15 + 10 + 5 + 20 = 50. Step 2: 100 − 50 = 50 books.

items.q: How many more ladybirds were found than spiders and worms together?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Ladybird 12, Spider 2 and Worm 4. Step 1: spiders and worms together: 2 + 4 = 6. Step 2: 12 − 6 = 6 minibeasts.

sets.title: Match the chart, and word problems

items.q: Favourite fruit: Apple 8, Pear 5, Plum 10, Kiwi 3. Which bar chart shows these numbers?
items.e: C matches every number (the scale goes up in 2s). A: two bars are the wrong way round; B: a bar is on the line below (it should be halfway between two lines); D: one bar is one line too high.

items.q: Minibeasts found: Ant 15, Worm 25, Snail 10, Slug 35. Which bar chart shows these numbers?
items.e: A matches every number (the scale goes up in 5s). B: two bars are the wrong way round; C: one bar is one line too high; D: one bar is one line too low.

items.q: Favourite colour: Red 40, Blue 25, Pink 60, Green 30. Which bar chart shows these numbers?
items.e: D matches every number (the scale goes up in 10s). A: two bars are the wrong way round; B: a bar is on the line below (it should be halfway between two lines); C: one bar is one line too high.
B matches every number (each symbol = 2). A: two rows are the wrong way round; C: a half symbol is drawn as a whole symbol; D: one row has a symbol too many.

items.q: Cakes sold: Mon 20, Tue 35, Wed 15, Thu 40. Which pictogram shows these numbers?
items.e: C matches every number (each symbol = 10). A: two rows are the wrong way round; B: a half symbol is drawn as a whole symbol; D: one row has a symbol too many.

items.q: Pets: Dog 15, Cat 10, Fish 20, Bird 5. Which pictogram shows these numbers?
items.e: A matches every number (each symbol = 5). B: two rows are the wrong way round; C: one row has a symbol too many; D: one row is missing a symbol.

items.q: Year 3 voted for their favourite fruit. How many more pupils chose grapes than pears?
items.e: Each circle = 2 votes, so half a circle = 1. Grapes: 5 × 2 = 10. Pear: 1 × 2 + 1 = 3. How many more means subtract: 10 − 3 = 7. (Half a circle is 1 here, because half of 2 is 1.)

items.q: Class 3B looked for minibeasts in the school garden. How many minibeasts did they find altogether?
items.e: Read each bar: ladybirds 9, worms 14, snails 6, spiders 11, woodlice 16. 9 + 14 + 6 + 11 + 16 = 56. (Reading 9 and 11 as 8 and 10 gives 54.)

items.q: How many more woodlice than snails did the class find?
items.e: Woodlice: 16. Snails: 6. How many more means subtract: 16 − 6 = 10. (5 is the number of grid spaces between the bars, not the number of minibeasts.)
Each star = 5 books. Harry has 5 stars: 5 × 5 = 25 books. 40 − 25 = 15 more books. (35 comes from counting the stars as 5 books.)
Amelia: 3 stars, 3 × 5 = 15. Isla: 2 stars, 2 × 5 = 10. Altogether: 15 + 10 = 25 books. (5 is the difference, or the number of stars.)

items.q: Art club has space for 15 children. How many more children can join Art club?
items.e: Art: 1 group of 5 and 3 more = 8. 15 − 8 = 7 more children. (Counting the group of 5 as 4 gives 7 children in Art, and a wrong answer of 8.)

items.q: How many more children go to Football club than to Choir and Chess together?
items.e: Football: 3 groups of 5 and 1 more = 16. Step 1: Choir and Chess together: 7 + 5 = 12. Step 2: 16 − 12 = 4.

items.q: How many fewer points has Hawk House got than Falcon House?
items.e: Falcon: 50. Hawk: halfway between 20 and 30, so 25. 50 − 25 = 25 points. (Reading Hawk as 20 gives 30.)

items.q: Each cake costs £1. How much money did the cake sale make on Tuesday and Wednesday together?
items.e: Each circle = 10 cakes, so half a circle = 5. Tuesday: 3 × 10 + 5 = 35. Wednesday: 1 × 10 + 5 = 15. 35 + 15 = 50 cakes, so £50. (Counting half a circle as 1 gives £42.)

items.q: There are 28 pupils in the class. Each pupil chose one sport. The bar for cricket is missing. How many pupils chose cricket?
items.e: Step 1: add the other bars: 10 + 7 + 6 = 23. Step 2: 28 − 23 = 5 pupils chose cricket. (Netball ends halfway between 6 and 8, so it is 7, not 6.)

items.q: How many snails did the two classes find altogether?
items.e: Find the Snails row: 7 and 15. Altogether means add: 7 + 15 = 22. (19 is 12 + 7, which adds down the Class 3A column instead.)

items.q: Each pupil has one pet. How many pupils are shown altogether?
items.e: Each square = 2 pupils, so half a square = 1. Dog 9, cat 6, fish 3, rabbit 4. 9 + 6 + 3 + 4 = 22. (Counting the squares gives 11. Leaving out the half squares gives 20.)

items.q: Leo wants to draw a pictogram of 40, 30, 50 and 20 votes. Which key needs the fewest symbols?
items.e: The bigger the key, the fewer symbols you draw. With 1 symbol = 10 votes, 40 votes is just 4 symbols. With 1 symbol = 2 votes it would be 20 symbols.

items.q: How many fewer chocolate ice creams were sold than vanilla and mint ice creams together?
items.e: Step 1: vanilla and mint together: 35 + 15 = 50. Step 2: chocolate is 45. 50 − 45 = 5 fewer.
